title: Vinegar Mutter a game made using chatgpt's new image model for the art.
author: Mekkablood

comments.author: Mekkablood
comments.body:
No vibe coding here, and a lot of photoshop work was done to help, but at its core all of the art was initially done with Chatgpt's new image model. This is my second game using ai for the art, and this model has taken it to the next level in regards to animations. 

Available to wishlist on Steam.

replies.author: bloodwolftico
replies.body:
A few questions if you dont mind:
- What would you say is the difference between the current model and the previous one? 
- How do you do the animations?
- Do you prompt for the same sprited in diff poses then cut the spritesheet and apply as needed? 
- What engine re you using?

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body:
1. Mostly consistence and prompt coherence

2. Using a picture it has generated (this is important), ask it to make a sprite sheet of different animations you want done. Scold it when it gets lazy and the art changes or just try again later.

3. UE5

replies.author: bloodwolftico
replies.body: Nice! TYSM. Your game looks fun btw.

replies.author: _JohnWisdom
replies.body: you gotta share the sprite sheet prompt because I would be as specific about grids and all but it would just do shit like 16x20 then 23x40 and what not. Like squished images and stuff. Anyways, amazing job here! Love the gameplay a tooon!

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: They're different all the time, the main thing is to make sure you're using a picture it generated as the reference. If it does something wrong tell it to stop being lazy and tell it what it did wrong. Also it's never going to be perfect(at least with this model). Every animation is going to require a ton of photoshop work typically.

comments.author: Dekker3D
comments.body:
That feels incredibly Heretic and I'm sure that's intentional. My main feedback is that you might want to break up the shapes of the room a little, so that it's not just a long and same-y looking hallway. Add a curve, or make it open up into a large room. Maybe add different textures to the areas to the side.

That said, I do love that you turned in this direction, it's pretty interesting.
